Daily Bank Reconciliation r2: D9, D10, safeguards and posting status — test-stage report (12 Oct 2026)

Scope of this stage - I built and tested the changes in my cloud workspace first. I then installed and verified them on the isolated test instance only (http://localhost/avenir_rv/, database avenir_restore_verify_20261011). - Not applied to the development system (avenir). It is still on r1, and its reconciliation tables are empty. Live is untouched. - Only dummy data and test logins were used. No real bank account was entered, no real statement was imported, and no accounting entry was posted. - I have stopped here. The next step needs your approval.

1. What changed and where

The changes (kit tf-bankrec-r2)

Change What it does now
D9: timing items in matching Listed and suggested. Timing items now appear with the open items and in the suggestions ("accepting clears the classification").
What a match keeps. Accepting a match clears the timing classification but keeps it on record: who classified it, when, the expected date, and a history (cleared → restored → cleared).
Undo. An undo restores the same classification, with the same classifier, time and expected date.
Two users. A match must name the timing classifications it clears. If another user classified the item a moment earlier, the match is refused with "Reload and confirm…".
D10: opening outstanding items Candidates. Ledger rows booked before an account's first day are listed as candidates, with their effect on bank − book.
Four eyes. The preparer proposes one as an opening outstanding item. A different person (the reviewer) accepts it.
What explains the opening difference. Only accepted items explain it. A row that clears later without being accepted never explains anything; the day shows "not an accepted opening item → insufficient data".
Counted once. Each date shows each opening item as outstanding or cleared on [date]. It counts as an opening item until the day it clears, then inside its match.
Partial clearing A match can clear part of an item. The rest stays outstanding, with an expected date. A later line completes it, and the partial match is kept as superseded. Undoing the completion makes the partial match active again.
Two users at once Guards:
  • one claim per matched or classified item, enforced by the database;
  • one change at a time per account;
  • version checks on statement lines and rates;
  • conditional updates for acceptance, decisions and reviews.
Result: duplicate matches, duplicate acceptance and double review are refused (409).
Changes after review What a record keeps. Each daily record keeps its snapshot, plus fingerprints of what it rests on: ledger rows, statement lines, rates, matches, explanations and opening items.
A later change flags the record "Changed since review — re-review needed" and names what changed. The reviewed snapshot is kept unchanged.
Corrections afterwards. Approving or posting a correction after the review is recorded as posting progress. It does not make the review out of date.
Exchange-rate differences Visible. Differences stay visible in each match.
Need an explanation. The 1 % suggestion tolerance never explains a difference: each needs a written explanation. A USD or JPY daily record cannot be prepared until the revaluation is explained.
From r1. Differences recorded under r1 without an explanation now show as "to explain".
Reconciliation status Clear states (section 2). A proposed or approved correction is never shown as "Reconciled"; the day reads "ledger not yet corrected". Pending postings are shown on:
  • the day;
  • the overview;
  • the corrections list;
  • reviewed daily records.

Files: Routes.php (3 routes added in the r1 group), the controller, Corrections / Matching / Rec / Schema / Statements, and the four views. Access.php is unchanged.

Database (schema version 2): - two new tables: brc_claim and brc_mark_event; - columns added to the reconciliation (brc_) tables only.

No other table is altered.

  10. Cloud: the races used two different preparer logins.
  11. The protections (claims, per-account lock, versions) do not depend on who the user is.
  12. "At the same time" means overlapping. The requests overlapped in time; the server takes one change per account at a time, so the second waits and is then refused cleanly.

  19. What is right: the status (not posted).
  20. What is not: the amount shown is the whole correction, not the part up to that date. It can be refined later.
  21. The old Bank Reconciliation screen is neither blocked nor detected. Its flags (bank_rec, bankst_flag) are not part of the daily-record fingerprint, so its use would not flag a reviewed record. See D7 for the rule I recommend.

  24. Why it matters: the reconciliation never borrows another day's rate, so a USD day with no rate shows "insufficient data".

D6 in detail: the daily-rate source

How the system picks a rate today: 1. The rate entered on Rates & transfers for that date and currency. 2. Otherwise, for USD only, the system's daily USD rate (daily_usd_rate) for that same date. 3. Never a rate from another date. Without a rate, the day shows "insufficient data".

My recommendation: one published source, entered every business day.

  • USD:
  • Which rate: the published USD telegraphic-transfer (TT) buying rate of the bank that holds the USD account, for that business date. Use the first rate the bank publishes that morning.
  • Who enters it: Accounts, on Rates & transfers, in LKR per 1 USD, with the source written as "‹bank› TT buying ‹date›".
  • Why the buying rate: it is the rate at which the bank turns Avenir's dollars into rupees. The USD → LKR transfers are done at it, so transfer and revaluation differences stay small and explainable.
  • JPY:
  • Which rate: the same bank's published JPY TT buying rate, entered per 1 JPY (if the bank quotes per 100 JPY, divide by 100), with its source.
  • Why it must be entered: there is no system JPY rate.
  • Weekends and holidays with entries: enter the last published rate explicitly for that date, with the note "carried from ‹date›". The system will not carry a rate forward by itself.
  • The system daily USD rate:
  • Keep it as a fallback only if you confirm it is taken from the same bank rate.
  • Otherwise I recommend switching the fallback off (a small change, needing your approval), so that every USD day uses a rate with a recorded source.
  • Why: in your export it exists on only 7 dates between 19 Aug and 7 Sep, with no source.
  • Month-end revaluation for the accounts: this follows Accounts' own policy (for example, a rate your auditors prefer). It is posted by Accounts, not by this module.

D7 in detail: keeping the old and new screens off the same periods

The rule. Once an account's ledger mapping is confirmed in the new workflow, its first day is the boundary for that bank ledger account: - From the first day onward, it is reconciled only in the new workflow. - The old screen is not used for that ledger account for any date on or after the first day. - Dates before the first day stay with the old screen.

Guard, recommended before live (needs your approval; not built): 1. The old screen refuses to mark rows of a mapped ledger account dated on or after its first day, and points to the new screen. 2. The new screen warns if any row of a mapped account, dated on or after the first day, carries old-screen flags. 3. After one parallel month, the old menu is withdrawn for mapped accounts.

Today's position. In your export, none of the bank ledger rows dated June–November 2026 carry old-screen flags; only a few future-dated rows (dated 2030) do. Those are among the existing irregularities, and I left them untouched.
